name: Slide deck
description: Seven starting slides: title, agenda, three content slides, a decision and next steps. Pi keeps one idea per slide and puts the detail in the speaker notes.
instructions: Before you write, ask who the audience is and how long the talk is, unless the Session already says. Fit the deck to the length, about one slide for every two minutes, adding or removing content slides, and set the talk length in <meta name="duration" content="15m"> so the presenter's timer shows it. Keep one idea per slide: a headline that states the point as a sentence, then at most three short lines, one chart or one table. Put the detail, the numbers behind it and what to say in that slide's <aside class="notes">. Keep deck.html with one <section> per slide, each with its <aside class="notes">, and keep deck.css; change the words, not the layout, unless a slide needs another shape. Draw charts as inline SVG from real numbers in the Session, and leave a slide out rather than invent data. End with the decision you need and the next steps with owners and dates. People see one slide at a time, drawn at 1280 by 720 and scaled to fit, so size text for that and keep each slide inside it. To build a slide up, mark the parts with data-step, or data-step="2" to set their order: they appear one per click or arrow key, and a part that has appeared has the data-shown attribute, which CSS can animate. CSS animations run each time a slide shows, and a script can listen for the slide event on its <section>. Only you edit slides: when someone asks in a comment on a slide to shorten, split, move, duplicate or delete it, change deck.html and publish again.
